name: detached-triggers-controlled
whatItDemonstrates: Three detached triggers sharing one handle, with the tooltip's open state and active trigger fully controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange`/`triggerId` and a plain button that opens the tooltip programmatically on trigger-2.
stateManaged: controlled — `useState` wrapping `open` (boolean) and `triggerId` (string | null); synced back through Root's `open`, `onOpenChange`, and `triggerId` props; `onOpenChange` reads `eventDetails.trigger?.id` to track the active trigger, and a plain HTML button sets `triggerId('trigger-2')` + `setOpen(true)` to open programmatically
nonTrivialInteractions: three detached `Tooltip.Trigger` elements (ids `trigger-1`/`trigger-2`/`trigger-3`) linked to one `Tooltip.Root` via a module-level handle from `Tooltip.createHandle()`
`onOpenChange(isOpen, eventDetails)` mirrors open state and extracts the active trigger id from `eventDetails.trigger?.id ?? null`
plain `<button>` opens the tooltip programmatically by setting both `triggerId` and `open` state

Divergence between variants (not styling): the tailwind variant uses aria-label="Controlled tooltip" on all three triggers, while the css-modules variant uses aria-label="Trigger 1"/"Trigger 2"/"Trigger 3"

name: detached-triggers-full
whatItDemonstrates: Three detached triggers passing distinct `payload` strings through one typed handle, with per-trigger popup content rendered via the function-as-a-child pattern and animated position/size/content transitions between triggers using `Tooltip.Viewport`.
stateManaged: none — no React state in the demo; `Tooltip.Root` manages open state internally (uncontrolled) and exposes the active trigger's `payload` through its function-as-a-child render prop
nonTrivialInteractions: module-level typed handle `Tooltip.createHandle<React.ReactNode>()` shared by all three detached triggers
each trigger passes a distinct `payload` string; Root's `({ payload }) => ...` render prop renders it as the popup content

`Tooltip.Positioner` sized with `--positioner-width`/`--positioner-height`/`--available-width` CSS variables and given `top/left/right/bottom/transform` transitions so the popup animates position between triggers

`Tooltip.Viewport` animates content switches using `data-activation-direction~='left'|'right'` selectors on `data-current`/`data-previous` child containers, with translate/opacity transitions and `data-instant` escape hatches

name: detached-triggers-simple
whatItDemonstrates: A single detached `Tooltip.Trigger` rendered outside its `Tooltip.Root`, linked by a handle created with the static `Tooltip.createHandle()`, showing a basic delete-button tooltip.
stateManaged: none — no React state in the demo; `Tooltip.Root` manages its own open state internally (uncontrolled)
nonTrivialInteractions: `Tooltip.Trigger` is a sibling of (not a child of) `Tooltip.Root`; they are linked by a module-level handle from `Tooltip.createHandle()`
hover/focus on the detached trigger opens the root's popup through the handle

name: hero
whatItDemonstrates: A toolbar of three icon buttons (Bold, Italic, Underline), each wrapped in its own uncontrolled `Tooltip.Root` under a shared `Tooltip.Provider`, showing basic hover/focus tooltips with arrows.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — three sibling `Tooltip.Root` components each manage their own open state internally; no `open`/`defaultOpen` props and no React state in the demo
nonTrivialInteractions: each tooltip is fully assembled inline: Root > Trigger + Portal > Positioner > Popup > Arrow
three independent Roots share one `Tooltip.Provider` so their open delays are grouped
hover- and focus-open on each trigger; `aria-label` on each trigger matches its tooltip content per the docs' accessibility guidance
